Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨5,\,3t+2,\,2⟩,\,b=⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩,\,c=⟨1,\,4t,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠ABC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/2c81d48afacc4ac5e81ab501bc713009ea4425451fcf8dbf414672aeadbb1679.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA} & =a-b \\  & =⟨5,\,3t+2,\,2⟩-⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{BC} & =c-b \\  & =⟨1,\,4t,\,3⟩-⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}=4$, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC} & =4 \\ 4\cdot 0+2\cdot t+0\cdot 1 & =4 \\ 0+2t+0 & =4 \\ 2t & =4 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA} & =⟨4,2,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{BC} & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}}{|\overset{\to }{BA}||\overset{\to }{BC}|} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{20}\cdot \sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{100}} \\  & =\frac{4}{10} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{5})≈{66.42}^{∘}.
$$
html:
Note that the position vectors of the points A, B and C are

a=⟨5,3t+2,2⟩,b=⟨1,3t,2⟩,c=⟨1,4t,3⟩.

The triangle △ABC is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠ABC=θ.

First, we find the components of BA→ and BC→: BA→=a−b=⟨5,3t+2,2⟩−⟨1,3t,2⟩=⟨4,2,0⟩BC→=c−b=⟨1,4t,3⟩−⟨1,3t,2⟩=⟨0,t,1⟩

Now, since BA→⋅BC→=4, we can solve for t, as follows:

BA→⋅BC→=44⋅0+2⋅t+0⋅1=40+2t+0=42t=4t=2

So, BA→=⟨4,2,0⟩,BC→=⟨0,2,1⟩.

Next, the cosine of the angle between BA→ and BC→ is

cos⁡θ=BA→⋅BC→|BA→||BC→|=442+22+02⋅02+22+12=420⋅5=4100=410=25.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(25)≈66.42∘.
